_comment: MASTER SYLLABUS TEMPLATE — Populated from PDF for Senior Six Subsidiary Mathematics.

competencies: The learner applies the knowledge of probability theory in predictions and decision-making processes.
The learner applies differentiation techniques in optimisation and analysing rates of change to interpret their significance in real life.
The learner applies integration techniques to solve problems involving areas, accumulation of quantities and other real-world applications.
The learner analyses concepts of random variables to model real-world situations in various contexts for informed decision making.
The learner interprets binomial and normal distributions for analysis of data patterns and trends in real-world contexts.
The learner analyses problems involving rates of change for prediction of alterations in various natural and social phenomena over a period of time.
values: honesty, uphold and defend the truth at all times
justice and fairness in dealing with others
integrity; moral uprightness and sound character
attitudes: appreciation of mathematics as a means of communication

themes.theme_description: The learner applies the knowledge of probability theory in predictions and decision-making processes.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies the knowledge of probability theory in predictions and decision-making processes.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: estimate the chances of occurrence of two related events for prediction and decision making in real life situations (k, s, u, v/a, gs).
evaluate conditional probabilities for two related events to predict outcomes and make reasoned decisions. (k, s, u, v/a, gs)

must_cover: Laws of probability and set theory
types of events (Mutually exclusive and independent events)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In group discussions, learners review: i) sample space. ii) Outcome (event). iii) Experimental and theoretical probabilities. iv) Laws of probability and set theory. v) Probability situations “AND” and “OR”. vi) types of events (Mutually exclusive and independent events).
In groups, learners discuss how to generate possibility space using tree diagrams and explore the use of permutations and combinations.
Through Think-Pair-Share, learners relate set theory to probability theory, design a contingency table and use it to determine the chance of occurrence of different events in different situations.

Collaboratively, learners explore tree diagrams (restricted to two pickings) to solve conditional probability problems involving real-world contexts such as business (e.g. customer behaviour analysis), healthcare (e.g. diagnostic tests) and quality control in manufacturing.

In pairs, learners use in - class experiments such as drawing with and without replacement (restricted to two pickings) to demonstrate how conditional probability works in practice; deepening the understanding of their use in real-world contexts.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they review the terms and laws applied in probability of two related events. Take note of learners’ ability to: i) listen attentively with comprehension ii) use numbers and measurements accurately iii) exhibit respect for humanity and environment.
In a conversation evaluate learners’ ability to generate sample space using different methods and determine probabilities.
Assess learners’ write-ups or diagrams and check for accuracy and validity of the probabilities obtained using various methods of solving a societal problem.

Observe learners as they discuss and explore conditional probability. Document learners’ ability to: i) plan and conduct investigations, ii) sort and analyse information, and iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.

Probe learners and judge their ability to: i) apply tree diagrams or otherwise, to represent conditional probability; and ii) apply conditional probability in various fields using real-life scenarios.
Assess the learner’s presentation or written report and check for correct use of the tree diagram or formula and accuracy of calculations in solving problems.

practicals.title: Drawing Experiments
practicals.description_verbatim: In pairs, learners use in - class experiments such as drawing with and without replacement (restricted to two pickings)

topics.core_competency: The learner applies differentiation techniques in optimisation and analysing rates of change to interpret their significance in real life.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: explore the gradient of a curve at a point to deduce derivative of a function in analysing real world problems. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
formulate functions from real life situations for optimisation. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)
apply the knowledge of differentiation to solve real-world problems to make informed decisions. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)

must_cover: derivatives of linear, quadratic and cubic functions

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through Think-Pair-Share, learners deduce that gradient of the tangent line at a point on the curve equals the derivative at a point.
In groups, learners discuss and determine the derivatives of linear, quadratic and cubic functions 0 < n < 4 (positive integers only)
Through induction, learners in groups, determine the second derivative of functions using the first derivative.
Learners, in groups, discuss and apply the following formula in different situations d(ln x)/dx = 1/x (Proof of the formula not needed)
Through discovery, learners in groups determine the value(s) of x for which the first derivative is 0 i.e. dy/dx = 0

Through group discussions, learners determine the value of x for which the function is either minimum or maximum to determine the maximum and minimum values of given functions e.g. Profit functions, Cost reduction functions.
Learners, through Think- Pair- Share, formulate functions from real-life situations for optimisation.

Through guided discovery, learners: i) Determine turning points of the quadratic curve by differentiation. ii) Investigate the nature of turning points (Maximum or Minimum points) using the sign change or second derivative methods. iii) Determine the intercepts to sketch the quadratic curves iv) Apply differentiation concepts to growth, optimization of resources, velocity, displacement and acceleration, etc v) explore and give justification why dr/dt = v(t) and dv/dt = a(t).

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss the derivative of a function paying attention to their ability to: i) work with others to generate ideas. ii) suggest and develop new solutions iii) showcase creativity and innovativeness
Probe learners and evaluate their ability to differentiate linear, quadratic and cubic functions and determine the gradient function.

Assess learners’ written work to find out the correctness of the: i) derivative at a point. ii) derivatives of linear, quadratic and cubic functions. iii) second derivatives of functions. iv) use of the formula d(ln x)/dx = 1/x

Observe learners as they determine the maximum and minimum values of given/formulated functions. Focus on their ability to: i) plan and carry out investigations ii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness iii) evaluate different solutions
Converse with learners and examine their ability to: i) explain and distinguish between maximum and minimum values of functions ii) formulate functions from real life situations for optimisation.
Assess learners’ write ups for correctness and accuracy of: i) value of x for which the function is either minimum or maximum. ii) the maximum and minimum values of given functions.

Observe learners as they apply differentiation concepts. Focus on learners’ ability to: i) talk confidently and explain ideas clearly, ii) suggest and develop new solutions, and iii) exhibit hard work and self-reliance.
Converse with leaners examining their ability to: i) determine intercepts and sketch curves; and ii) apply differentiation concepts to real-life situations
Assess the learners’ written work to find out the correctness of: i) calculations and nature of turning points in curve sketching, ii) application of differentiation in real-life situations.

themes.theme_description: The learner applies integration techniques to solve problems involving areas, accumulation of quantities and other real-world applications.

topics.core_competency: The learner applies integration techniques to solve problems involving areas, accumulation of quantities and other real-world applications.

prerequisites.notes: Differentiation and integration are linked as inverse operations.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: relate integration and differentiation to integrate definite and infinite integrals including natural logarithms in real-world contexts. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
apply integration concepts to determine areas under curve, velocity and displacement functions in real-world scenarios. (k, u, s, v/a, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Through guided discovery, learners explore how differentiation and integration are inverse operations; linking the two concepts.
Through problem-based learning (PBL), learners use the integration formula ∫ 1/x dx = Inx + C to solve real-world problems, such as accumulated costs in economics (proof not required).
Using guided discovery approach, learners: i) sketch quadratic curves ii) explore how to calculate the area between a curve and the x-axis in a given interval, a line and a curve, two curves.

Using collaborative learning, learners apply integration in real-world scenarios such as obtaining velocity and displacement functions from given variable acceleration and velocity functions in physics and engineering contexts.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they integrate definite and infinite integrals including natural logarithms, noting their ability to: i) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, ii) use mathematics to justify and support decisions, and iii) exhibit respect for humanity and environment.
Probe learners to evaluate their ability to apply differentiation and integration as inverse operations in practical scenarios in economics, engineering etc.
Assess learners’ write-ups for correct application of integration techniques, including step-by-step solutions to solve real-world problems.

Observe learners as they apply integration concepts, noting learners’ ability to; i) sort and analyse information, ii) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, and iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness
Converse with learners and examine their ability to apply integration techniques to determine areas under curve, velocity and displacement functions

Assess learners’ written work for; i) accurately created sketches of quadratic curves, ii) detailed calculations of areas under the curves and the x-axis in a given interval, a line and a curve, two curves, iii) accuracy of velocity and displacement functions, and iv) correct conclusions of the real-world applications.

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses concepts of random variables to model real-world situations in various contexts for informed decision making.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: utilise the concept of discrete random variables to solve real-world problems such as quality control and game theory. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
employ the concept of continuous random variables to solve real-world problems in contexts. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

must_cover: mode and median of a discrete random variable

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners perform experiments in class, such as flipping coins, rolling dice or drawing cards from a deck, and list the possible outcomes to identify a random variable and discrete random variable.

Through guided discovery, learners record the outcomes of a random variable X e.g. the number of heads obtained from tossing two coins and determine the corresponding probabilities to generate probability distributions.

Through group discussions, learners explore the properties of probability distribution function (p.d.f) of a discrete random variable, and use these properties in determining probabilities of events to sketch the graph of a p.d.f.
Through Think – Pair-Share, learners determine the mode and median of a discrete random variable.
In groups learners discuss and analyse the data from case studies, calculate probabilities, expected values, variances and standard deviation using the formulae and present their findings.
In groups, learners perform experiments such as time taken to complete a task, distance travelled, or speed of an object to understand the concept of continuous random variable.

Through project-based learning, learners discover the properties of continuous random variables by collecting data and interpreting their probabilities in a real-world context. For example, heights and weights of students in class, temperature in a room, etc.
Through Think-Pair-Share, learners distinguish between continuous and discrete random variables.
In pairs, learners calculate probabilities of continuous random variables of events in real world situations like: heights and weight of students in class, and temperature in a room.

In group discussions, learners use knowledge of integration to compute the probabilities, expectation, variance and standard deviation of a continuous random variable in order to analyse data using the formulae and present their findings to the class

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they, apply concepts of discrete random variables noting their ability to: i) interact effectively with others ii) look for patterns and make generalizations iii) exhibit social harmony.

Engage learners in a conversation and evaluate their ability to: i) determine the probabilities for each outcome ii) relate total probability to the outcomes. iii) calculate expectation E(X), variance Var (X) and standard deviation of a discrete random variable.
Assess learners’ written work for: i) accuracy of the possibilities generated, ii) accuracy of mode and median, and iii) correctness of calculations of E(X), Var(X) and standard deviation.

Observe learners as they apply concepts of continuous random variables taking note of their ability to; i) use imaginations to explore possibilities. ii) work with others to generate ideas, and iii) show respect for humanity and environment.

In conversation with learners, examine their ability to: i) apply the properties of continuous random variables; and ii) use integration to compute the probabilities, expectation, variance and standard deviation.

Assess learners’ write ups and project reports and check for correctness and accuracy of: i) application of properties of continuous random variables, ii) the difference between continuous and discrete random variables, and iii) calculations of probabilities, E(X), Var(X) and standard deviation of a continuous random variable.

themes.theme_description: The learner interprets binomial and normal distributions for analysis of data patterns and trends in real-world contexts.

topics.core_competency: The learner interprets binomial and normal distributions for analysis of data patterns and trends in real-world contexts.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: interpret a binomial distribution to solve real-world problems involving success-failure scenarios. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
interpret the normal distribution to solve real-world problems involving normally distributed data (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

must_cover: mean, mode, and variance of a binomial distribution

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups, learners conduct an experiment such as rolling a die 10 times and recording number of times ‘a 4 or higher number appears’, record their results in a table, showing the number of successes for each set of 10 trials to review theoretical and experimental probabilities. They can also do the same with a coin.

Through group discussions, learners explore the meaning of the following terms as associated with Binomial distribution; i) number of trials (n), ii) number of successes (x), iii) probability of success in a single trial (p), iv) probability of failure in a single trial (q), and v) probability of exactly k successes in n trials P(X = k).
Learners, in pairs, perform a binomial experiment and use it to determine probabilities of success and failure in a number of trials (n ≤20).

Through Think-Pair-Share, learners apply Binomial formula or use mathematical tables to determine probabilities of real-life binary outcomes such as Return on Investment (Profit/loss), Disease Diagnosis (positive/negative), and Match outcome (Win/Loss.

In groups, learners discuss mean, mode, and variance of a binomial distribution and its application in real-world such as expected return on investment, expected number of defects in a production process, optimise inventory based on the most likely demand, measure the uncertainty of outcomes, etc.
In groups, learners discuss normal distributions, standard normal distributions and their properties for better comprehension of the concept.

In groups, learners discuss standardization of random variables and use of cumulative normal distribution tables/calculators to: i) determine probabilities, ii) compare data points to the mean, iii) compare distributions, and iv) visualise data spread.

In groups, learners discuss the applications of normal distribution function to solve societal problems such as data visualization, economic forecasting, analysing treatment outcomes, modelling communication networks, etc.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they discuss concepts of binomial distribution, putting emphasis on learners’ ability to: i) interpret and interrogate mathematical data, ii) interact effectively with others, and iii) exhibit creativity and innovativeness.
Converse with learners and evaluate them as they: i) explain terms associated with binomial distribution; and ii) determine probabilities using the formula or mathematical tables.

Assess learners’ written work and check for: i) the correctness of terminologies, ii) correct substitutions in the formulae iii) accuracy of the values of mean, mode and variance of a binomial distribution obtained, and iv) correct use of calculator or tables.

Observe learners as they discuss normal distribution, noting the learners’ ability to: i) interact effectively with others, ii) work with others to generate ideas, and iii) exhibit justice and fairness in dealing with others.

Dialogue with learners to establish their ability to: i) standardise a random variable, ii) apply the parameters; mean (μ), standard deviation (σ), variance (σ²) associated with the Normal distribution, and iii) apply the normal distribution function to solve societal problems

Assess learners’ write ups work for coherence and accuracy of: i) properties of the Normal distribution, ii) application of parameters; Mean (μ), Standard deviation (σ) and Variance (σ²) in calculations of probabilities, and iii) Calculation of parameters (de-standardisation) to solve societal problems.

practicals.title: Binomial Experiment
practicals.description_verbatim: In groups, learners conduct an experiment such as rolling a die 10 times and recording number of times ‘a 4 or higher number appears’

topics.core_competency: The learner analyses problems involving rates of change for prediction of alterations in various natural and social phenomena over a period of time.

prerequisites.notes: Understanding of derivative as instantaneous rate of change.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: formulate differential equations using various real-life scenarios to make informed decisions. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)
analyse real world situations using differential equation techniques. (k, u, v/a, s, gs)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In group discussions, learners review equations such as y =x² to: i) determine the first derivative; and ii) discuss a derivative being an instantaneous rate of change to explore the concept of a differential equation.
Through Think- Pair- Share, learners discuss how to identify and form a differential equation.
Through Think- Pair – Share, learners explore general and particular solution of a first order differential equation using integration.
Through guided discovery, learners discuss solving differential equations with separable variables related to natural occurrences.
Through exploration, learners in pairs, use the internet and other sources to discuss practical applications of differential equations in real world and present to the whole class.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe the learners as they review the first derivative and discuss differential equation. Note their ability to: i) interact effectively with others, ii) identify problems and ways forward, and iii) exhibit justice and fairness.
Dialogue with learners, analysing their ability to identify and form differential equations.
Assess learners’ written work, taking keen interest in the accuracy of formulated differential equations.

Observe the learners as they discuss and search for applications of differential equations; noting their ability to: i) interact effectively with others, ii) sort and analyse information, and iii) demonstrate hard work for self-reliance.
Converse with learners, judging their ability to: i) solve first order differential equations with separable variables and ii) analyse applications of differential equations in real life.
Assess the learners’ written work, focusing on the relevancy and correctness of the applications of differential equations in real life.

suggested_uses: use the internet and other sources to discuss practical applications
